$comment: Paired flag A/B for the two write-path fixes to SCARE's jumpy heat constraint envelope (eval_full_v2_20260728: SCARE max_t_k tail peak-to-peak >20 K on 58.9% of matched tasks vs 0.0% for single_level, and 1242 temperature violations vs 20-26).
Mechanism under test, two independent levers on the SAME failure:

(1) enable_cp_heat_guard_plant_tracking - the CPHeatOutletGuard only ever writes DOWN, so while the L3 kernel parks the CP near zero the outlet cools for reasons the ceiling did not cause; the AIMD recovery credited that cooling to itself and ratcheted +0.05/poll open-loop, and the next commit spent the whole accumulated headroom in one tick (measured 372 K -> 407.55 K on branch-371-114, then a halving, ~6 s period). Bounding recovery to one step above the STANDING regulation closes the loop.

(2) enable_cp_regulate_slew_limit - the sector="cp" path in apply_regulate had only a ceiling (clamps DOWN), unlike the electricity and heat paths which already bound their steps. Symmetric per-write bound on kernel commits; the guard's cp_heat_outlet_relief bypasses it.
Arms: {} = both on (new defaults); then each lever off alone; then both off = eval_full_v2_20260728 behaviour.

Judge on: legacy_metrics__max_t_k__max minus __min (the swing), claims__constraint_compliance detail temperature n_violations / worst_overshoot, events__cp_heat_outlet_relief / cp_regulate_slew_limited, and that heat served fraction + PWSF + outcomes__cp_generation n_active do NOT regress (the slew limit delays a legitimate ramp by design).

NOTE: this campaign does not isolate enable_cp_own_supply_netting, which removes the r_{k+1} = R - r_k oscillator upstream of both levers. Expect these two to stop binding once that lands; run this A/B against a fixed netting setting.
name: ab_cp_thermal_oscillation
